premises.text: Valuable status reports and similar group communications stay trapped in person-to-person email, causing less-informed decisions, duplicated work, and lost money
premises.evidence_span: these communications that are loaded with valuable business information are sent by email from one person to another, and the rest of the company can't access them

premises.text: Managers set who reports, schedule, and templates in ~30 seconds; ThinkFuse prompts writers so reports are consistent, timely, shared, without manager harassment
premises.evidence_span: all we need to know is who you want status reports from, when you want them, and what information they should include

premises.text: Shared recipient lists and Twitter-like project follow give stakeholders ongoing access to current and prior reports
premises.evidence_span: each of these people can follow a project just as easily as they can follow someone on Twitter

premises.text: Aggregated status reports map a business graph of people-project relationships searchable to find expertise, client relationships, and office location across the company
premises.evidence_span: Using status reports, we're mapping the relationships between people and projects in a company

value.text: Everyone understands the whole organizational puzzle so people and resources align
value.evidence_span: each person understanding the entire puzzle and where their pieces fit in

causal_links.evidence_span: decisions are less informed, work is duplicated, and ultimately, companies lose money
making status reports more accessible, by making them more consistent, and more powerful
ThinkFuse helps you leverage that information

notes: Email inaccessibility consequences folded as one knowledge problem (§4.1.6). Setup/prompting and follow/share kept as status-product facets; business-graph search/expertise discovery split as separately framed leverage module. Beta praise treated as traction (§4.2).
